THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 07.04.2025, ALONG WITH MACA.2300/2017, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 2025:KER:29811 MACA NO.2300 OF 2017 &
MACA NO.1990 OF 2017  4  JUDGMENT

The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.378/2014 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Vatakara, is the appellant herein in MACA No.2300/2017 and the 3rd respondent therein is the appellant in MACA No.1990/2017 (For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2. The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 02.11.2018.

According to the petitioner, on 02.11.2018 at about 12.30 p.m., while he was riding a motorcycle, a bus bearing reg.no.KL-60-C-7973 driven by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner hit against the motorcycle and as a result of which, he fell down and sustained serious injuries.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner, the 2nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P.
is Rs.45,00,000/-.
The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimonies of PWs 1 and 2 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A27.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.33,73,466/- rounded to Rs.33,73,470/-
and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner and 3rd respondent preferred these appeals.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

sentences.text: Heard Sri.Abu Mathew, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Sri.George Cherian, the learned Senior Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.

10. The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid 2025:KER:29811 MACA NO.2300 OF 2017 &
MACA NO.1990 OF 2017 insurance policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
According to the learned Senior counsel, the notional income and the compensation awarded on different heads are on the higher side.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.
According to him, the petitioner was working as dredging worker, earning Rs.30,000/- per month, but the Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.9000/-.
11. The learned counsel has relied upon the evidence of PW2 and Ext.A24 to prove the income of the petitioner.
PW2 was the President of Vatakara, Port Manual Dredging Workers Co-operative Society.

entities.text: Port Manual Dredging Workers Co-operative Society
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He would swear that the petitioner was working as manual dredger in vatakara port and that he used to get a daily wage of Rs.780/- and a monthly income of Rs.20,208/-.
Though he claimed that there are documents in the office to prove the income received by the petitioner from dredging, no such documents were produced.
However, from PW2 and Ext.A24 it is revealed that the petitioner was a member of Vatakara, Port Manual Dredging Workers Co-operative Society and he was engaged in dredging sand from river.

entities.text: Vatakara, Port Manual Dredging Workers Co-operative Society
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 12. As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance 2025:KER:29811 MACA NO.2300 OF 2017 & MACA NO.1990 OF 2017 Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2013 will come to Rs.9000/-.

sentences.text:
Therefore, considering the fact that the petitioner was engaged in dredging sand from river and in the light of the evidence of PW2, his notional income is fixed at Rs.12,000/-,
for the purpose of computing the loss of disability.

13. In the accident the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
 Type III C open distal 1/3rd femur left with compromised distal vascularity and had to be amputated below knee.
14.
Ext.A6 disability certificate shows that the petitioner suffered 80% permanent physical disability.
It was issued by the medical board.
The Tribunal, however, scaled down the percentage of disability of the petitioner to 60%, without assigning valid and cogent reasons.
The law is settled that, if the Tribunal is not satisfied with the disability certificate produced by the petitioner, the remedy is to refer him to a medical board or higher Authority.
(See Manikantan G. v. Janardhanan Nair and Others, 2021 (5)KHC 305).

entities.text: Manikantan G. v. Janardhanan Nair and Others, 2021 (5)KHC 305
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having not done so, the Tribunal was not justified in scaling down the percentage of disability from what is shown in the disability certificate.
I do find any grounds to disbelieve the said disability and as such the permanent 2025:KER:29811 MACA NO.2300 OF 2017 & MACA NO.1990 OF 2017 physical disability of the petitioner is fixed as 80%.
15. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 37 years.

Therefore, 40% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd v.

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.24,19,200/-.
16. Towards loss of earning, the tribunal has awarded Rs.108888/- being the income for 12 months @Rs.9000/-.

Since the notional income of the petitioner is re-fixed at Rs.12000/-, towards loss of earning he is entitled to get a sum of Rs.1,44,000/-(12000 x 12 months)
17.
Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.1,00,000/-.
Towards 'loss of amenities of life' Rs.50,000/- was awarded.

According to the learned counsel for the petitioner,
the compensation awarded on those heads are on the lower side.
18. The petitioner sustained very serious injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 10 days and his left leg above knee was amputated.

Because of the injuries sustained, the percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that 2025:KER:29811 MACA NO.2300 OF 2017 & MACA NO.1990 OF 2017 the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings' and 'loss of amenities of life' are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.1.50,000/-, and Rs.1.50,000/- respectively.
19.
Towards 'extra nourishment', the tribunal has not awarded any amount.

Hence, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, Rs.10000/- is awarded on the aforesaid head.
20.
Towards cost of prosthesis the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.15,00,000/-.
The learned senior counsel appearing for the 3 rd respondent would argue that Rs.15,00,000/- awarded by the Tribunal towards expense of artificial limb and its maintenance is on the higher side.
The learned counsel for the petitioner has relied upon Exts. A16, A17 and A25.
As per the above tax invoices and letter the cost of one prosthesis varies from Rs.14,483/- Rs.40,000/-.
The learned counsel has produced fresh quotations also.
In Ext.A16 the cost of a prosthesis is shown as Rs.3,02,000/-.
In Ext.A17 it is stated that the carbon sockets of the prosthesis is to change upon physical change and its cost will be Rs.40,000/-.
It further states that the foot shell need to be changed usually once in every two years and its cost will be Rs.25,000/-.
Cosmesis need change usually once in every two years and its cost will be Rs.15,000/-.
Servicing of knee joint may require once in every 2025:KER:29811 MACA NO.2300 OF 2017 & MACA NO.1990 OF 2017 five years and its cost will be Rs.30,000/-.
Therefore, from Ext.A17 it appears that annual cost of maintenance will come to Rs.26,000/- in additional to replacement of carbon socket on physical change.

Considering the fact that the age of the petitioner on the date of the accident was 37, I hold that the petitioner can be awarded a sum of Rs.6,00,000/- towards the cost of prosthesis and Rs.5,00,000/- towards the cost of its maintenance, and as such towards cost of prosthesis and its maintenance he is entitled to get a sum of Rs.11,00,000/-.
21.
No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
